2609.35627.title: Can LLMs Value the Right Evidence? Evidence-Value Misalignment in Dynamic Medical Diagnosis
2609.35627.paper_summary: A correct diagnosis reached from insufficient or misleading evidence can pose a clinical hazard, yet outcome-based accuracy may reward such lucky guesses. We call this mismatch between diagnostic decisions and the value of available evidence Evidence-Value Misalignment (EVM). To disentangle evidential grounding independently from diagnostic accuracy, we introduce MedEVM, a dynamic benchmarking environment comprising 1,050 cases across 24 disease systems. Observations arrive turn by turn, requiring models to continuously calibrate its decision by deciding whether to wait for more evidence or submit a diagnosis. Across 9 LLMs, four interesting patterns are observed. (1) Miscalibrated evidence tracking. Making a diagnosis often fails to calibrate evidence sufficiency, even in more capable models, and even worsens in reasoning mode. (2) Misaligned diagnosis submission. Confidence in the correct diagnosis often fails to ensure timely submission despite sufficient evidence. (3) Evidence order matters. Reordering the same evidence changes diagnoses even when model confidence remains similar. (4) Misleading evidence remains influential. Added misleading evidence redirects diagnoses even after prior evidence becomes sufficient. We further verify that EVM predicts errors and that preventing premature submission improves accuracy. These findings motivate Evidence-Verified Diagnosis Harness (EVD-Harness). It decouples diagnosis generation from submission through an offline Contrastive Diagnostic Wiki and three online control stages, namely observation management, proposal and witness verification, and diagnosis submission control. Across five LLMs, EVD-Harness improves accuracy by 12.0--51.1 percentage points while mitigating EVM-related failures. Our results demonstrate that verifying evidential support before submission can make diagnostic decisions more reliable.
2609.35627.paper_summary_zh: 正確的診斷如果是基於不足或誤導的證據，可能會造成臨床危險，然而基於結果的準確性可能會獎勵這種幸運的猜測。我們稱這種診斷決策與可用證據價值之間的不匹配為證據價值不一致（EVM）。為了獨立於診斷準確性來理清證據基礎，我們引入了MedEVM，這是一個動態基準環境，包含1,050個案例，涵蓋24個疾病系統。觀察結果逐回到達，要求模型不斷校準其決策，決定是等待更多證據還是提交診斷。在9個大型語言模型（LLMs）中，觀察到四個有趣的模式。(1) 證據追蹤不準確。即使在更強大的模型中，做出診斷通常也無法校準證據的充分性，並且在推理模式下甚至會惡化。(2) 診斷提交不一致。對正確診斷的信心通常無法確保及時提交，即使證據充分。(3) 證據順序重要。重新排序相同的證據會改變診斷，即使模型信心保持相似。(4) 誤導性證據仍然具有影響力。添加的誤導性證據會重新導向診斷，即使先前的證據已經充分。我們進一步驗證了EVM預測錯誤的能力，並且防止過早提交可以提高準確性。這些發現促使了證據驗證診斷工具（EVD-Harness）的誕生。它通過一個離線對比診斷維基和三個在線控制階段，即觀察管理、提案和見證驗證，以及診斷提交控制，將診斷生成與提交解耦。在五個大型語言模型中，EVD-Harness將準確性提高了12.0至51.1個百分點，同時減少了與EVM相關的失敗。我們的結果表明，在提交之前驗證證據支持可以使診斷決策更可靠。
